extracted.intended_audience: general readers and people studying jokes/humor (comedians, linguists, educators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and descriptive criteria for constructing and performing a knock-knock joke: its call-and-response format, five-line script, phonetic/wordplay devices, and delivery considerations. Useful for writers, performers, and analysts of this specific joke form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-and-response format
rubrics_metrics.description: The knock-knock joke is a structured word play joke that uses call and response. The joke is performed cooperatively by the speaker and the listener in a call and response format as they create a scene depicting a visitor knocking at a door.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance requires cooperation: the speaker initiates with 'knock-knock' and the listener must reply with the scripted lines to create the scene. The format is central to the joke's functioning; failure to follow call-and-response undermines the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependence on prior exposure and linguistic knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The joke is dependent on the speaker and the listener having previous exposure to the joke's format and enough general and linguistic knowledge to understand what is being referenced in the punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the audience doesn't know the format or lacks necessary linguistic/cultural knowledge, the wordplay/punchline will not register. Design jokes for an audience familiar with the format or provide scaffolding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard five-line structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard knock-knock joke has five lines of dialogue: Introduction, Scripted reply, Setup, Response, Punch line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhering to the five-line structure preserves expectations that the punchline will re-interpret earlier lines; variations exist but the five-line form is the conventional template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line 1 — Introduction ('knock-knock')
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first line, the speaker plays the role of someone knocking at the listener's front door by saying 'knock-knock'. The line is an example of onomatopoeia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line 1 is often spoken with a stylized fall (the second syllable in a lower pitch than the first). Delivery/intonation on this line contributes to recognizability and comedic timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line 2 — Scripted reply ('who's there')
rubrics_metrics.description: In the second line, the listener's response of 'who's there' has them play the role of someone inside their own home as the speaker knocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This scripted reply establishes the conversational frame; it signals to both parties that the knock-knock template is in effect and invites the setup line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line 3 — Setup (a word or phrase identifying the 'visitor')
rubrics_metrics.description: The third line is the point that a person at the door would provide their given name or some other identifier. The joke traditionally uses a name for the third line, but any phrase can be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a proper name is traditional, but creative phrases, objects, or homophonic material can be used to set up the pun. If an inanimate object is referenced, it is inferred that a person is using the object as a name rather than literally being the object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line 4 — Response (repeat phrase + 'who')
rubrics_metrics.description: The fourth line is normally when the person at home repeats the phrase, followed by the word 'who', to request more information. This mimics someone asking for clarification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listener's repetition is the pivot that creates the phonetic material the punchline will exploit. Clear repetition helps the audience parse the elements that the punchline will reinterpret.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line 5 — Punch line (word play/pun that breaks the scenario)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fifth line breaks from the imagined scenario of a person knocking on a door and delivers a punch line using word play based on the phrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The punchline typically reinterprets the setup/response via homonymy or phonetic blending. Examples: 'Lettuce. Lettuce who? Lettuce in!' or 'Tank. Tank who? You're welcome!' The fifth line often changes the meaning of the third and fourth lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive humor from homonyms/conflation
rubrics_metrics.description: Knock-knock jokes are a type of word play joke, which derive their humor from the conflation of homonyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful jokes exploit identical or similar-sounding sequences (homonyms/homophones) so the punchline produces an unexpected reinterpretation. Choose words/phrases with viable phonetic doubles or near-homophones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit phonetic structure for extended puns or sentence blends
rubrics_metrics.description: Some knock-knock jokes end by repeating the third line, using its phonetic structure as a pun to be the start of a new sentence; in this case, the content of the third line is spoken quickly to blend its sound into the rest of the phrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two strategies: (1) blend the third line into the punchline by rapid speech so it forms part of a larger sentence (e.g., 'Lettuce in!'); (2) take advantage of the phonetic structure of the fourth line so the fifth line is a response to the newly created phrase (e.g., 'Tank' → 'Tank who?' → 'You're welcome!'). Timing and phonetic stress are crucial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intonation and stylized fall matter for delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'knock-knock' line is often spoken with a stylized fall, a type of stylized intonation where the second syllable is said in a lower pitch than the first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use characteristic intonation (minor third fall) to cue the audience and enhance comedic effect. Delivery prosody contributes to recognizability and the joke's rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional/trivial content risk and audience reception
rubrics_metrics.description: After peaking in popularity, knock-knock jokes received push-back from critics who saw them as unfunny, pseudo-intellectual, or pathological, though they remained popularly known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that knock-knock jokes can be perceived as childish or groan-inducing; their acceptability depends on context, audience expectations, and self-aware delivery (e.g., intentionally 'bad' jokes vs. clever wordplay).
